speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the format of the Government's after-action review (AAR) on COVID-19; and (b) whether it plans to share the AAR's findings or recommendations with the public.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the first phase, which was from the start of the outbreak to August last year, we focused on containing the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Thereafter, when we had vaccinated a high proportion of people in Singapore, we shifted our approach to learn to live with the virus.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Likewise, only a few weeks ago, at the Administrative Service Appointment and Promotion ceremony, the Prime Minister said we will be throwing away valuable lessons for which we have paid dearly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can he also share how many participants are envisaged to participate in this AAR, will it be a whole-of-Government exercise?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: He will do a thorough exercise in reviewing the Government's response, which is our intent, to learn thoroughly and rigorously from what we have experienced so far, in order that we can do better for the next pandemic, which will surely come.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This was also the approach we took when we reviewed the lessons from SARS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Which is why, as Minister Ong Ye Kung said just now, we had put in place a DORSCON framework, we set up the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Likewise, we will learn many lessons, many useful lessons from COVID-19, particularly the first phase of the experience.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will use these lessons to improve our response for the next pandemic.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I ask the Minister whether the AAR will also include a more detailed assessment of how our $100 billion COVID-19 spending has been spent?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have said, it will look at a whole range of issues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are many things that the AAR will cover.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the focus will really be on issues of strategic and national importance which will enable us to learn and do better and be better prepared for the next pandemic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am sure everyone will agree that it is in our shared interest to achieve that objective.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do that with regard to all areas of spending and, where relevant, we will put out information on how the monies are spent.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But let the AAR focus on the more strategic and important issues that will enable us to be better prepared for the next pandemic.
